title: Fixed Size Array - Initilizer Lists, Changing to take <T, size>
description:
You may have noticed with the `std::vector` is initlized with somthing like {1, .....}. This is called a `std::initializer_list`. To copy from a `std::initializer_list` to a int*, you can use std::copy(<list>.begin(), <list>.end(), <ptr>); (this needs you to include algorithm). To make a initlizer list-inited class, you make the constructor just take a std::initializer_list, and thats the constructor.
### Moving size into the template.
Templates have more features than I taught previously, the additional features being:
1. Defaults: You can put a = after a template param (just like a function arg) to make it default to that value.
2. Non-typename: You can put any type in a template, EG `template <int X>`, then X will be the number passed.


---
## Assignment
1. Make the class take a int (defaulting to 1) in the type_name.
2. If the int is passed (and >= 1), then allocate size just like normal, and otherwise, allocate the `.size()` of the initializer (or 1 if empty), then copy the elements.
3. Make a overload of the constructor for no list passed, and create a array size of S.
